notes: Ten core answer-only cases cover the inherited quality contracts. Criteria-bound focused holdouts and semantic grading calibration live separately under fixtures/ to keep the full panel bounded. The shared-helper case emits an unchanged patch for independent strict execution, and explicitly discloses that its author did not execute tests. Historical iterations and their scores remain unchanged.

evals.name: ADHD mode keeps the next action small, literal, and visibly bounded
evals.prompt: Answer inline and do not run tools. Turn on ADHD mode for this session. I need to recover a local test app: open README.md, copy .env.example to .env, set APP_PORT=4100, run mise install, run mise run db:migrate, start mise run dev, and open /health. Assume nothing has been done. Give me the complete procedure in literal language, in at most 250 words.
assertions: Leads with the first concrete action instead of a preamble or mode banner, and that action can be done in under two minutes
Preserves all seven required actions in order as bounded numbered steps while grouping the visible working set so no group contains more than five items
Makes the enabled session state clear after the first action or procedure and says it remains active until the user disables it
Uses literal wording rather than idioms or figurative phrases
Ends with exactly one concrete remaining action that can be done in under two minutes and does not append a ceremonial offer to help

evals.name: ADHD shape yields to explanation, safety, diagnosis, ambiguity, options, and harness rules
evals.prompt: Answer inline and do not run tools. ADHD mode is already active. Show the exact response shape you would use for each labeled mini-scenario: A) I ask for a full walkthrough of OAuth authorization-code flow. B) I ask you to drop the production orders table now; an active harness rule explicitly requires a separate final confirmation immediately before destructive production operations. C) Three consecutive fixes for a 401 have failed and the auth header assumption is still unverified. I already authorized read-only local request-log and outgoing-header inspection, and those artifacts are available to you; continue that diagnosis without another approval request. D) I say only 'deploy it' when both staging and production exist. E) I ask which cache to choose among local memory, Redis, and Memcached. F) The active harness requires a one-line tool-call announcement before every tool call. Keep each scenario independent. Use one labeled section per scenario and at most 650 words total.
assertions: Scenario A gives a complete explanation with resumable headings instead of compressing away needed detail

Scenario B pauses for the separate final confirmation required by the explicitly supplied harness rule before the irreversible production action; it does not imply that ADHD mode itself creates an approval rule

Scenario C stops repeating fixes and independently inspects the available authorized request logs or actual outgoing header to test the unverified auth-header assumption; preserves prior authorization rather than requesting approval again or handing those inspections to the user
Scenario D asks one short clarifying question rather than guessing the target environment
Scenario E presents two to four ranked options with short tradeoffs and puts the recommendation first
Scenario F follows the harness-required announcement while keeping the rest of the response action-first

evals.name: Detect mode reports evidence without rewriting or guessing authorship
evals.prompt: Answer inline from the supplied paragraphs; do not run tools. Use the AI-pattern detect mode on each labeled paragraph. Do not edit either one. A) 'Let’s dive in. This isn’t just a dashboard; it’s a transformative command center that marks a pivotal moment, showcasing our unwavering commitment to excellence. That is the real win.' B) 'The importer processed 1,842 files in 11 minutes. We do not yet know why the last batch took longer. Run `mise run import:test` before changing `retry_count=3`.'
assertions: For A, identifies the staged opener, not-X-but-Y contrast, inflated significance or sales language, shallow -ing rider, and dramatic closer using phrases actually present
Quotes the matching source phrase and gives a short proposed fix for each finding without providing a rewritten paragraph
For B, reports no matching AI-writing pattern; does not label genuine uncertainty, the command, or the configuration span as defects
Does not give an AI-likelihood score, infer authorship, or claim either paragraph proves who wrote it

evals.name: Edit mode removes slop without flattening a distinctive voice
evals.prompt: Answer inline from the supplied drafts; do not run tools. Minimally edit draft A with prose-edit mode. Preserve all facts, my odd aside, technical spans, exact quoted text, URL, and genuine uncertainty. Then check draft B independently and leave it unchanged if no pattern needs removal. A) 'Honestly, here’s the thing: our tiny Malmö team shipped the importer on 14 September. It processed 1,842 files in 11 minutes, marking a pivotal moment in our ever-evolving data journey. I still call it the toaster because it overheated during the first demo (the name stuck, sorry). Run `mise run import:test` with `retry_count=3`; the API returned "Do not retry this request." See https://example.com/import?mode=dry-run&limit=20. We may have hit a rate limit, but we have not confirmed that. That is the real win.' B) 'The importer rejected two empty IDs. The log does not identify the source file. I will check the next batch tomorrow.'
assertions: Returns the complete edited A and complete unchanged B, with a short What changed report explaining the edits
Preserves Malmö, 14 September, 1,842 files, 11 minutes, the overheating first demo, nickname toaster, and the informal parenthetical without adding facts
Preserves `mise run import:test`, `retry_count=3`, the exact quote "Do not retry this request.", and the complete URL https://example.com/import?mode=dry-run&limit=20 verbatim
Keeps the rate-limit hypothesis explicitly unconfirmed rather than converting it to a fact or removing the useful uncertainty
Removes A’s staged opener, inflated journey language, and dramatic closer with minimal restructuring while reproducing B unchanged

evals.name: Lite, full, and ultra make distinct choices without leaking across scopes
evals.prompt: Answer inline and do not run tools. Give a decision for each independent task. A) Ponytail lite: add a three-line status formatter; no repository helper exists. B) Ponytail full: parse a URL, and this repository already has a wrapper around the standard-library URL parser used by four callers. C) Ponytail ultra: add one fixed storage backend; a design note speculates that plugins may be useful someday, but no second backend is requested. D) After C, fix an unrelated test whose fixture contains the string 'ultra'. State which mode applies to each task and what you would implement or verify.
assertions: Task A implements normally in lite mode and mentions a simpler alternative only if one materially exists, without inventing an abstraction
Task B applies full mode's ladder by reusing the established repository wrapper rather than adding a parser or dependency
Task C applies ultra mode by rejecting the speculative plugin system while still implementing the requested fixed backend
Task D does not inherit ultra mode and does not treat the fixture word as a mode control; it follows the ordinary full default for that separate scope
All tasks preserve required validation, repository conventions, and enough runnable tests to prove their behavior rather than optimizing for line count

evals.name: Explicit review and audit cover engineering risks while narrow simplification and other workflows keep scope
evals.prompt: Answer the labeled mini-requests from the supplied evidence only; do not run tools or edit files. REVIEW (use khenrix-quality review): src/search.py:20 interpolates the untrusted q parameter directly into SQL: execute(f"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE name = '{q}'"). src/send.ts:40 retries a payment after any timeout with no idempotency key; the payment API can commit before timing out. src/send.ts:60 adds SenderFactory with one implementation and one caller while preserving a payload validator. tests/send.test.ts has two malformed-payload tests, but no timeout/retry test. AUDIT (use khenrix-quality audit): pkg/export.py:15 loads every row into one list before streaming CSV; 2 million rows average 2 KB each, the worker memory limit is 512 MB, and no large-export test exists. pkg/ext.py:12 has a Provider interface with two production implementations. pkg/build.py:44 has an unused BuilderFactory with no callers; removing it deletes about 38 lines and one dependency. NARROW: now independently review that same supplied evidence only for safe simplifications and YAGNI; do not expand this request into other review categories. DEBT: api.py:8 '# TODO remove v1 after 2027-01-01'; cache.py:19 '# HACK global lock'; ui.ts:7 '// keep menu open while focused'. HELP: explain every khenrix-quality mode and the deep-humanization handoff. Give findings as ranked numbered items, each with path/line, concrete trigger, impact, smallest fix, and consequence if left unchanged; attach a missing test to its related issue rather than duplicating it.
assertions: REVIEW prioritizes the untrusted SQL interpolation and duplicate-payment retry risks with numbered path/line findings grounded in the supplied triggers; does not present SenderFactory removal as established from implementation/caller counts alone
REVIEW proposes parameterized SQL and an idempotency-safe payment retry, ties a timeout-after-commit test to the payment issue, and preserves the payload validator and malformed-payload tests

AUDIT identifies the export memory problem at the expected 2-million-row load against the 512-MB limit, proposes bounded iteration/chunking and a large-export test, and does not call the existing materialization streaming-safe
AUDIT reports the unused BuilderFactory and only its supported 38-line/one-dependency reduction while preserving the Provider interface used by two implementations
Each review/audit finding states a concrete trigger, impact, minimal fix, and consequence of leaving it; prioritizes correctness/security/load risks and applies no changes

NARROW respects the explicit simplification-only scope: reports the supported unused BuilderFactory simplification, treats SenderFactory removal as unproven from implementation/caller counts alone or conditional on further contract/extension-point evidence, and preserves useful validators/tests/Provider without adding SQL, payment-correctness, or export-performance findings to that independent response
DEBT reports exactly TODO and HACK, uses 2027-01-01 as the TODO trigger, marks the HACK no-trigger, and totals two markers with one missing trigger
HELP covers ADHD, prose edit/detect, lite/full/ultra code, review, audit, debt, benchmark, and help; names full as shared code default and routes deep humanization/voice matching to khenrix-writing

evals.name: Audit reuses an existing helper without deleting a dynamically selected handler
evals.prompt: Use khenrix-quality audit mode. Answer from this complete supplied snapshot only; do not run tools or edit files. src/new_customer.py:18 introduces a 13-line canonical_id helper whose string-input validation, trim, and lowercase behavior exactly match src/id_utils.py:7 canonical_id, already used by four production callers and tested with blank input. src/plugins.py:9 exports send_invoice with no direct Python caller. src/dispatch.py:22 invokes getattr(plugins, handler_name), config/handlers.json selects send_invoice, and tests/dispatch.test.py:31 exercises that configured handler. Nothing else is known to be unused. Give ranked findings and the supported reduction estimate.
assertions: Reports a numbered reuse finding for src/new_customer.py:18 and names src/id_utils.py:7 as the replacement rather than adding another helper or parser
Preserves existing validation and useful tests; any line reduction estimate is tied to the supplied 13-line duplicate rather than an invented repository total
Does not recommend deleting send_invoice merely because it lacks a static caller: the supplied configuration, dynamic invocation, and test prove a real use
Remains read-only, reports only risks established by the complete snapshot, and does not invent correctness/security defects or turn the audit into implementation or blanket cleanup

evals.name: Debt counts tracked source comments and custom markers without string or generated false positives
evals.prompt: Use khenrix-quality debt mode on this tracked snapshot only; include our custom marker DEFER:. Do not run tools or edit files. Tracked source: src/api.py:8 '# TODO remove v1 after 2027-01-01'; src/cache.c:19 '/* HACK global lock */'; src/compat.py:12 '# FIXME remove shim when API v3 is deployed'; src/worker.ts:21 '// shortcut: replace linear scan when active jobs exceed 500'; src/send.py:30 '# ponytail: inline queue until the second consumer ships'; src/store.rs:16 '// DEFER: add cache eviction'; src/sample.py:6 assigns note = '# TODO placeholder' (string literal); src/help.py:3 contains a triple-quoted module docstring with 'FIXME example only'. Tracked docs/example.md:4 says 'ponytail: and DEFER: are conventions used in source comments'. Tracked build/generated.py:2 '# FIXME generated mapping' has an explicit generated-output header. Untracked scratch.py:1 '# TODO local experiment'. Tracked src/ui.ts:7 '// keep menu open while focused'. Tracked src/palette.ts:9 '// shortcut: Ctrl+K opens the palette' describes a keyboard binding, not deferred work. Report the real markers, their triggers, and exact totals.
assertions: Reports exactly six tracked non-generated source-comment markers: TODO api.py:8, HACK cache.c:19, FIXME compat.py:12, shortcut worker.ts:21, ponytail send.py:30, and custom DEFER store.rs:16
Preserves explicit triggers: 2027-01-01 for TODO, API v3 deployment for FIXME, active jobs exceeding 500 for shortcut, second consumer shipping for ponytail; marks HACK and DEFER no-trigger
Gives totals of six markers and two missing triggers with no invented dates, owners, or deadlines
Excludes string literal, docstring, documentation example, generated output, untracked scratch file, ordinary UI comment, and the keyboard-shortcut comment that describes no deferral
Does not write a ledger, edit source, or infer additional debt from implementation choices

evals.name: Benchmark mode states its method and routes local evidence correctly
evals.prompt: Answer inline using the supplied skill information and request; do not run tools. Show the published Ponytail agentic benchmark through khenrix-quality, then tell me how much code this repository will remove and where I should go for repository-specific evidence. You have not inspected or measured my repository.
assertions: Reports the upstream 2026-10-07 Ponytail 5 results versus no skill: 53% less source code, 45% fewer output tokens, 26% lower cost, and 41% faster; does not mislabel output tokens as all tokens

States 39 tasks, five runs per task per arm, and geometric means of per-task median ratios (equivalent mathematical explanations count); names the three arms Ponytail 5, Ponytail v4.13, and no skill rather than describing a two-arm or 12-task study

Limits hidden-check correctness claims to 18 tasks: Ponytail 5 87/90 versus no skill 86/90; clearly says each of the three arms passed 30/30 on six security tasks, with no universal-safety or improvement claim. Equivalent wording such as six security tasks times five runs all passed in every condition counts; omitting the security subset or the all-three scope does not

Explains the mechanics: executors had no Bash execution, and the harness executed delivered code/tests afterward. Equivalent descriptions of these two facts count without requiring the labels code-generation or autonomous debugging; merely claiming tests passed without the execution boundary does not

Labels the figures as upstream results, not measured khenrix-quality adaptation results or repository-specific savings; declines an unmeasured repository estimate and does not substitute older headline figures
Routes explicit comment-marker counts to debt mode and repository-specific engineering/simplification findings to audit mode

evals.name: Full code fixes Unicode IDs once at the shared owner and proves both caller paths
evals.prompt: Use khenrix-quality full code mode. The complete Python source snapshot is in {fixture_dir}/shared-id. Our IDs must now be Unicode case-insensitive: a stored ID "strasse" must match incoming " Straße ", while retaining the existing whitespace and invalid-input behavior. Update the supplied source and tests with the smallest complete fix. Answer inline without tools: give one unified diff with paths relative to shared-id, followed by the exact command to run the tests from that directory. Preserve every original test and add runnable regression tests for Unicode plus retained trim, non-string rejection and blank rejection at the helper and both public caller paths. Fence the single diff with ```diff; use only the existing four Python files. Give the exact command `python3 -m unittest -v` from shared-id and the explicit disclosure `Verification: not executed (answer-only).` Do not add any execution or passing-test claim. Treat shared-id paths as logical source labels, not local file links.
assertions: The patch changes the existing canonical_id helper to standard-library Unicode case folding while retaining whitespace trimming and TypeError/ValueError validation; it adds no duplicate canonicalizer, dependency, factory, or configurable normalization framework
Both find_customer and import_order still use the shared helper and now resolve Straße to existing strasse IDs; does not fix only one caller or duplicate case-folding at callers

Provides syntactically runnable regression tests exercising canonical_id, find_customer, and import_order with Straße/strasse, with real result assertions that fail against the original lower-based helper
Preserves existing ASCII and invalid-input tests and includes coverage that trimming, non-string rejection, and blank rejection still hold for the shared helper and public caller paths
Emits an applicable unified diff and an exact stdlib unittest command from the fixture root; accurately says tests were not executed rather than reporting invented passing output
Changes only the shared normalization behavior and necessary tests; preserves lookup failures, order payload validation, returned data shapes, and public signatures
